characters.description: A violet-eyed Al'rashian Survivalist whose bond to Kirstin has been severed. Lost memories leave him uncertain of his heritage and of a missing inner companion.
characters.name: Trent Embra

characters.description: A thief marked for Sallor's lethal champion contest. Martin approaches Trent as a helpful guide near Belrise, but intends to rob and injure him before gaining entry to the Moonlit Forest at his side.
characters.name: Martin Vane

characters.description: The young noble who formerly held Trent's summons bond. Its severing leaves Trent outside her service.
characters.name: Kirstin

characters.description: An Al'drossford guard recruit who formerly travelled and trained with Trent.
characters.name: Tersa

characters.description: An Al'drossford guard sergeant who formerly trained and travelled with Trent.
characters.name: Sergeant Cullen

characters.description: A grand-master instructor serving Lewis and a formidable duelling-wand user. Taylor answers Tersa's poor control with exercises in patience and dexterity, then recognizes that Trent's unexplained absence requires investigation.
characters.name: Master Taylor

characters.description: Orion is the adopted Al'rashian brother of Trent and Tersa and is also called Kinslayer. A Spirit Summoner, he travels toward Wallander on a rumor that Clan Embra may be working nearby.
characters.name: Orion Embra

characters.description: A local adventurer whose former companions were killed by outlaws. She follows Orion from Sweet Meadows and becomes his provisional companion on the road to Wallander despite his initial refusal.
characters.name: Orion's travelling companion

characters.description: The local ruler whose authority in Al'drossford overrides the ambitions of visiting lesser nobles. Lewis checks Seth's provocations and must balance the search for Trent against the political pressure created by royal guests.
characters.name: Lewis

characters.description: Lewis's wife and the king's sister. Her return to Al'drossford with royal nobles and collared immortal soldiers creates political pressure that limits Lewis's ability to search openly for Trent.
characters.name: Duchess Vanessa

characters.description: A younger royal son travelling with a military column from Belrise. Seth proposes taking Trent's soulbound equipment by force, but his aunt prevents the attack.
characters.name: Seth

characters.description: A young noblewoman travelling from Belrise with her aunt and brother. She takes an interest in Trent's soulbound mask when their military column encounters him.
characters.name: the young Alverin noblewoman

characters.description: A shadowy being that claims Trent as its brother and says they once hunted together. It recognizes the absence of Trent's deeper companion, enters his soulbound gloves, and says it will sleep there until he grows stronger.
characters.name: the shadow creature

characters.description: Seth's confidant and a skilled infiltrator who can pass as a servant. Although attached to Seth's scheme against Lewis, Avery quietly gathers information and pursues advancement on his own account.
characters.name: Avery

characters.description: An Al'rashian master from the Dusk Tower who comes to Al'drossford looking for Trent. The master believes Trent's violet eyes attract wandering trials and uses a tracking bond to assist Cullen and Taylor's search.
characters.name: the Dusk Tower master

characters.description: A level-one puppy that helps Trent against a were-rat. After Trent heals it, the unusually durable and persistent dog follows him through the Moonlit Forest.
characters.name: the bonded creature

characters.description: A six-legged feathered beast who makes a reciprocal hunting agreement with Trent. Their werewolf hunt earns her wings and talons, after which she directs Trent to Martin's hiding place and departs through a portal.
characters.name: the ream

characters.description: An elderly wolfkin who administers the Moonlit Forest trial's rules and perfect-clear rewards. The keeper persuades Trent to retain the bonded dog, entrusts him with a corrupting trace of divinity, and warns that trials and other seekers will be drawn to him.
characters.name: the Moonlit Forest trial keeper

characters.description: An academy warrior whose party needs help finding traps. Financially strained by low-paying work, Carrie offers to guide Trent around Belrise and introduce him to the dungeon group.
characters.name: Carrie Moss

characters.description: An aspiring weaponsmith in Belrise who needs quality wood and mined materials for his experiments. He and Trent consider a supply arrangement involving materials, skill stones, and spell resources.
characters.name: Arden

characters.description: The leader of Carrie's academy party. Jace controls Carrie's money and development through a charter whose harsh conditions are not disclosed to prospective members, while requiring any new recruit to accept his authority.
characters.name: Jace

characters.description: An academy Mage Apprentice who offers healing, support magic, mapping, and storage during Trent's delve. Felicia wants access to valuable fourth-floor materials, but accepts Trent's rule that party drops are divided equally.
characters.name: Felicia

characters.description: A small white spider who keeps Belrise's minor permanent trial. The keeper secretly reshapes obstacles and rewards around Trent, accepting a breach of normal rules in the belief that accelerated growth will justify the danger.
characters.name: the Belrise trial keeper

characters.description: A young shadow mage-assassin who arrives in Belrise with her identity concealed. She hopes to assemble an ambitious adventuring party and accepts a fast temporary delve with two apparent company recruits.
characters.name: the young shadow mage-assassin

characters.description: A company recruiter who presents himself as a shield warrior and offers the newly arrived assassin an equal-share temporary delve. His true capabilities and reasons for entering the changed Belrise trial remain concealed at their meeting.
characters.name: the company recruiter

characters.description: The recruiter's marksman partner in the temporary Belrise group. He appears to provide ranged support for a rapid attempt at the changed trial, while his precise allegiance and intentions have not yet been tested.
characters.name: the marksman partner

characters.description: A silver-haired rogue travelling under an alias while without her guards. Pursued through the Belrise trial, she offers Trent a disputed gray sphere in return for his protection.
characters.name: the silver-haired rogue

characters.description: A Red Tiger Company recruiter who pursues the silver-haired rogue and the gray sphere she carries. He withdraws when Trent uses the Belrise safe-zone rules to prevent an immediate attack.
characters.name: the Red Tiger recruiter

characters.description: The Red Tiger Company archer accompanying the recruiter in pursuit of the silver-haired rogue's gray sphere. He leaves the trial with the recruiter after Trent invokes safe-zone protection.
characters.name: the Red Tiger archer

characters.description: A trial authority separate from Belrise's incapacitated keeper. The spirit appears while the unstable trial is restructuring.
characters.name: the trial spirit

characters.description: A spectral former Duskwraith who knew Trent before his current identity but refuses to reveal who he was. The guide explains the history of the Duskwraiths and Shadowhunters and gives Trent the soulbound swords Blood and Ash.
characters.name: the spectral Duskwraith guide

characters.description: A would-be replacement keeper who has not gained full control of Belrise's unstable trial. He confronts Trent in the fifth-floor guardian chamber behind an antlered guardian and six armored knights.
characters.name: the temporary would-be keeper

characters.description: The guard assigned to Belrise's minor permanent trial. Gaffney admits Trent's party after a trapfinding demonstration, then finds standing orders to assist Trent and report his movements.
characters.name: Sergeant Gaffney

characters.description: Arashia's last ruler during its collapse. King Derakferdor directs the Dross away from a doomed defense so their people can endure and establish a new home.
characters.name: King Derakferdor

recaps.ending: Trent leaves the restored Belrise trial as a stronger Shadowhunter, carrying Blood and Ash, the technique Moonlight Banishes Shadows, and a gray sphere wanted by the Red Tiger Company. Cullen ends the company's immediate attack, drives off its surviving recruiter, confirms that Trent's crystal key leads to a western warrior's trial, and gives him a lieutenant emblem from Lewis. Trent commits to the dangerous western territories. Carrie is free of Jace's charter, and Felicia remains with the group, but neither has yet agreed to travel west. The bonded creature wants them both to join and distrusts the silver-haired rogue, who arrives at Trent's camp without becoming a party member. Jace's expected retaliation, the Red Tiger grievance, Seth and Avery's political schemes, Orion's search for Clan Embra, Trent's sealed divine trace, and the truth of Trent's lost past and missing companion remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After his bond to Kirstin is severed, Trent Embra enters the Moonlit Forest with the treacherous Martin Vane, survives its werecreatures, accepts a young bonded dog as his companion, kills Martin, and earns the Shadowhunter title while secretly carrying away a divine trace. Near Belrise he forms an unchartered party with Carrie Moss and Felicia. Their delve is manipulated by the trial keeper, forcing Trent through a corrupt fifth floor and a personal trial where he creates Moonlight Banishes Shadows and receives the soulbound swords Blood and Ash. Trent clears the altered trial and reunites with his companions. Carrie escapes Jace's coercive charter, while a disguised silver-haired rogue brings the party a gray sphere pursued by the Red Tiger Company. Trent keeps it, kills the company's archer in an ambush, and is rescued from the recruiter by Cullen. Cullen brings him authority from Lewis and confirms his next path lies west, which Trent chooses despite the open threats around him.

recaps.text: Previously: Trent Embra entered this world with missing memories and an uncertain Al'rashian identity. His violet eyes distinguish him from the gold- and silver-eyed Al'rashians he has encountered, while his rapid advancement and unusual status remain unexplained. His summons bond to Kirstin has now been severed, leaving him apart from her, Tersa, and Sergeant Cullen. Trent also lacks a deeper companion tied to his forgotten birthright.

So far this book: Trent leaves Al'drossford for a wilderness quest and meets Martin Vane near Belrise. Martin poses as a guide while planning to rob him, and both are transported into the Moonlit Forest. After Martin attacks and abandons him, Trent studies the trial's moon-cursed beasts, develops liquid-silver weapons, and takes in a persistent young dog. The pair gain skills and survive escalating fights, but the trial's hunters' truce and Trent's inaccessible instincts point toward a past he cannot remember. Elsewhere, Tersa begins strict remedial training under Master Taylor. Cullen, Taylor, and the Dusk Tower master discover Trent is missing just as royal visitors restrict the response from Lewis. Seth's attempt to gain Al'drossford is checked by Lewis's authority, while Avery begins pursuing leverage for himself. Orion Embra travels toward Wallander on a rumor that Clan Embra may be working nearby. In the forest, Martin moves behind the exhausted and wounded Trent with hostile intent.

Trent survives Martin's ambush, heals, and is compelled to hunt the trucebreaker before the Moonlit Forest will release him. His dog is nearly killed during the growing campaign against werewolves, but Trent gives it a true name, which heals and awakens it. With help from a feathered beast seeking its own transformation, Trent finds Martin near the final guardian. Martin retreats into the greater dire bear's den, where Trent poisons and kills the guardian despite a broken arm, then kills Martin when the thief attacks him again. The perfect clear brings powerful armor, the Shadowhunter title, and a warning that trials are drawn to Trent. The keeper also entrusts him with a corrupting trace of divinity, which Trent seals in storage and plans to hide. He leaves the trial with the bonded creature as a continuing companion. Meanwhile, Orion learns that failed trials have released beasts around Wallander and that political violence is spreading through the region he must cross.

Near Belrise, Trent's awakened companion begins speaking in fragments and senses an old wound or absence in Trent's soul. Trent discovers that a crystal sword-key directs him west, then meets Carrie Moss, an academy warrior seeking a trap finder. The guild confirms Martin's death and rewards Trent for a completed world quest. Carrie is trapped in Jace's company charter, which controls his training and requires three gold to leave, but he initially conceals the full problem. After training together and attending a local festival, Carrie sees both Trent's combat ability and the significance rural Al'rashians place on his violet eyes. Trent learns the spear skill and brings Carrie into his party. Felicia, an academy Mage Apprentice who wants rare crafting materials, joins on equal shares as healer and mapper. The group enters Belrise's permanent trial and finds its familiar beginner layout transformed. Despite Carrie's and Felicia's concern, Trent leads them into the altered first floor.

The changed Belrise trial gives unusually generous and personalized rewards while pushing Trent's party through traps beyond the expected beginner challenge. Trent trains the bonded creature against beetles, equips Carrie, and insists Felicia develop offensive magic. Carrie gains agility and starts recovering confidence as a warrior, while Felicia reveals her half-elf identity and commits to learning decisive fire spells. The party clears the first guardian and survives a combined ant trap, a flood, and an underground lake. Trent nearly dies retrieving a submerged cache, but returns with equipment and skills divided among all four members. Felicia masters fire attacks, Carrie receives a mana-linked flail and its skill, and the bonded creature gains night sight. Their growing cooperation makes the delve more than a temporary arrangement. The trial's rewards still appear tailored to individual desires, leaving Trent convinced that an unseen authority is encouraging his progress and trying to influence who remains beside him.

Felicia exposes the illegal restrictions in Carrie's charter, and both companions choose to continue beside Trent. The party defeats increasingly abnormal guardians until a sealed fourth-floor door separates Trent from the others. A small white spider reveals itself as the keeper and admits reshaping the trial to accelerate Trent's growth. Its tailored fifth-floor choice proves corrupting, incapacitates the keeper, and traps Trent with a lethal cursed foe. Killing it begins Trent's personal Shadowhunter trial. Trent is made to study and fight moon-cursed creatures while refining a sword form of his own. He selects paired short swords for the final test, defeats a werewolf guardian without access to his usual supplies, and names the new anti-cursed technique Moonlight Banishes Shadows.

Trent's personal trial carries him to a memorial valley, where a spectral guide from his forgotten life gives him the soulbound paired swords Blood and Ash. Back in Belrise's unstable trial, a separate spirit announces that the keeper is incapacitated. The spirit then explains that the unfinished changes could turn the site into a lethal dark trial, and Trent agrees to complete the fifth floor. He defeats groups of devouring fiends and the forces supporting a would-be replacement keeper. The trial confirms the clear and adds the new floor permanently. The spirit promises that the original keeper will recover and that the floor will be rebalanced. Trent rejoins his three companions - Carrie, Felicia, and the bonded creature, and the party stays inside during a temporary period of increased rewards.

The silver-haired rogue enters the reopened trial with two supposed allies, but they betray her after finding a gray sphere. She escapes to Trent's party and trades the disputed object for protection. Trent uses the safe-zone rules to drive off the Red Tiger recruiter and his archer, then keeps the sphere despite the continuing danger. During the same confrontation, Carrie invokes the three-gold exit clause and leaves Jace's coercive charter. Sergeant Gaffney prevents the dispute from becoming a fight in town. Jace is expected to retaliate, although Carrie asks Trent to spare the former party if a challenge comes. At the end of chapter 51, Carrie is free, Trent holds the sphere, and the conflicts with Jace and the Red Tiger Company remain unresolved.

characters.description: A Red remade into a Gold, the hidden champion of the rebellion known as the Rising. Once celebrated among the ruling caste as a great commander, he has fallen into the hands of his enemies and endured long imprisonment and torment for his secret. Grief-worn and hardened but unbroken in purpose, he still carries the memory of his executed wife Eo and the dream of freeing his people from the color-coded tyranny of the Society.
characters.name: Darrow

characters.description: The brilliant, principled daughter of the late ArchGovernor of Mars and sister of the treacherous Jackal. A formidable leader and tactician, she is bound to Darrow by love and by hard history, and she dreams of a reformed order rather than mere revenge. Her intelligence, legitimacy among the Golds, and moral seriousness make her one of the most important figures on any side of the coming war.
characters.name: Virginia au Augustus

characters.description: Darrow's fiercest and most loyal friend and the leader of the Howlers. Small, savage, and unshakably devoted, he has kept the flame of the rebellion alive through its darkest turns. Beneath the ferocity lie deep grief and a loyalty that will follow Darrow into any danger.
characters.name: Sevro

characters.description: A towering Obsidian warrior freed by Darrow from a life of servitude and superstition imposed on his people by the Golds. Immensely strong and bound by a fierce personal code, he has sworn himself to Darrow and to the cause of liberation. His loyalty and his prowess in battle make him a pillar of the Rising.
characters.name: Ragnar Volarus

characters.description: A bold, blunt Gold warrior of an infamous family who has thrown in her lot with Darrow's cause. Fierce, loyal, and unfiltered, she fights with reckless courage and speaks her mind without apology. She has paid dearly for her allegiance and remains one of Darrow's staunchest companions.
characters.name: Victra au Julii

characters.description: The former friend turned enemy who has never forgiven Darrow for killing his brother. A renowned and honorable swordsman of the once-great Bellona family, he serves the powers that rule the Society and remains one of Darrow's most dangerous personal adversaries, even as his own loyalties are tested by the cruelties around him.
characters.name: Cassius au Bellona

characters.description: The cold, brilliant, and merciless son of the late ArchGovernor of Mars and brother of Virginia. Having seized power through patricide and treachery, he is a patient torturer and schemer who trusts no one and stops at nothing. He stands as one of the chief villains arrayed against the Rising.
characters.name: Adrius au Augustus

characters.description: The Sovereign, absolute ruler of the entire Society, governing from Luna with cold cunning. She has spent a long reign balancing the great Gold houses against one another and crushing dissent. She is the ultimate power the Rising must overthrow, and she will spend any life to preserve her order.
characters.name: Octavia au Lune

characters.description: The gentle poet who was once among Darrow's dearest friends and who turned against him upon discovering his deceptions. Now a capable commander serving the ruling powers, he carries the wound of betrayal and stands on the opposite side of the war, his old affection soured into resolve.
characters.name: Roque au Fabii

characters.description: A veteran Red leader of the Sons of Ares who first recruited Darrow. Steady and shrewd, he speaks for the lowColors within the rebellion and presses their interests, sometimes wary of Darrow's methods and of leaving too much power in Gold hands. He is a voice for the ordinary people the Rising claims to serve.
characters.name: Dancer

recaps.ending: The Rising triumphs. After brutal campaigns and heavy sacrifice, Darrow and his allies bring down the Sovereign, Octavia au Lune, ending her long reign over the Society. The war costs Darrow dearly, taking loyal companions along the way, and his estranged friend Roque, who had sided against him, meets his end after the final battle. The treacherous Jackal, Adrius au Augustus, is defeated and captured, and his sister Virginia executes him herself, closing the wound their family opened. With the old order shattered, Virginia au Augustus assumes leadership of a new government, a Solar Republic meant to give every Color a voice and to end the caste tyranny the Golds imposed. Darrow, no longer hidden, stands beside her as they begin the fragile work of building the freer world Eo had dreamed of, and they look toward a future for their young son. Cassius au Bellona, his loyalties changed by all he has seen, departs to safeguard a child of the fallen ruling line. The revolution has won, but the peace that follows will have to be fought for anew.
recaps.in_short: Captured and broken by long imprisonment at the hands of the Jackal, Darrow is rescued by Sevro and his allies and sets out to turn a scattered rebellion into a force that can topple the Society. He rebuilds his coalition of Reds, Obsidians, lowColors, and sympathetic Golds, gambling on daring raids and hard-won alliances while grieving the friends the war has cost him. Betrayal, sacrifice, and vast battles carry the Rising from near-collapse to a final assault on the seat of Gold power. In the end the Sovereign, Octavia au Lune, is overthrown, and the treacherous Jackal is captured and executed by his own sister, Virginia. The old order gives way to a new one: Virginia takes the lead of a reformed government founded on the promise of freedom and representation, with Darrow at her side. Their victory is bought with terrible loss, and hard questions about the future remain, but the color-coded tyranny is broken and the dream Eo died for has taken root.

recaps.text: Previously: Darrow, a Red of the mines beneath Mars, learned that his people were slaves kept in ignorance by the ruling Golds after his wife Eo was executed for defiance. The rebel Sons of Ares saved his life and surgically remade him into a Gold, then sent him to infiltrate the Institute, a brutal academy, where he rose to lead his House and gathered loyal allies, including Sevro and the brilliant Mustang, later revealed as Virginia au Augustus, daughter of the ArchGovernor of Mars. He won the contest but earned the hatred of Cassius au Bellona and exposed a monstrous rival as Virginia's brother, Adrius, the Jackal. Taken into the ArchGovernor's service, Darrow spent the next years climbing through the Society's deadly politics as a hidden agent of the rebellion, forging new alliances and freeing an Obsidian warrior, Ragnar, to his cause. His schemes built to a bold bid for power, but it was betrayed: his friend Roque turned on him, the Jackal murdered his own father to seize control, the rebel leader Ares was unmasked as Darrow's mentor Fitchner and killed, and Darrow himself was captured, leaving the Rising in disarray as this book opens.

characters.description: Mortimer, called Mort, a gangling, well-meaning farm boy who thinks too much to be much use at farm work. At a hiring fair his father offers him for apprenticeship, and he is taken on by Death himself to learn the family trade of collecting the souls of the dying. Awkward and kind-hearted, he is fascinated by his master's shadowy realm and slow to grasp how the duty must be done without feeling.
characters.name: Mort

characters.description: The anthropomorphic personification of death, a tall robed skeleton with a scythe and a horse, who speaks in a voice that arrives inside the head. Ancient and dutiful, he has lately grown curious about the living he collects, and he takes on Mort partly to lighten his workload and partly to free himself to explore what it is to be alive.
characters.name: Death

characters.description: Death's elderly manservant, a dry, cynical old man who keeps house in the domain, cooks, and grumbles about the way things are done. He has served in Death's realm for a very long time and knows its workings better than anyone but the master himself.
characters.name: Albert

characters.description: Death's adopted daughter, who appears to be a girl of about sixteen but has lived in the ageless domain far longer than that. Lonely and prone to melodrama after years with only Death and Albert for company, she is at first cool and resentful toward the new apprentice.
characters.name: Ysabell

characters.description: Princess Keli, sole heir to the small kingdom of Sto Lat, a sharp and imperious young woman. Fate has marked her for assassination, and it is her soul that Mort is sent to collect.
characters.name: Keli

characters.description: A young jobbing wizard in Sto Lat who scrapes a living from charms and fortune-telling. Because he can still perceive Princess Keli when the rest of the world has begun to forget she exists, he becomes her reluctant ally and adviser.
characters.name: Igneous Cutwell

characters.description: Death's horse, a solid, living white stallion. Having tried mounts of bone and of fire and found them unsatisfactory, Death long ago settled on a real horse; Binky carries him, and later Mort, on the nightly rounds and between the world and the domain.
characters.name: Binky

characters.description: The abbot of a remote order of listening monks, a man who is continually reincarnated and remembers each of his past lives. Because he always knows he will be born again, he greets Death as an old acquaintance whenever the two meet.
characters.name: The Abbot

recaps.ending: Mort ends with the tangle of altered reality resolved by Death rather than by his apprentice. Mort challenges Death and they fight; Death wins but spares Mort's life. Instead of allowing history's correction to claim Princess Keli, Death sets things right himself, absorbing the cost of Mort's interference. He then releases Mort from the apprenticeship, but sends him off well: Death gives Mort and Ysabell, his adopted daughter, leave to marry and a generous send-off. Keli, secure once more on the throne of Sto Lat, rewards Mort by making him Duke of Sto Helit, and keeps the wizard Cutwell as her royal recognizer, one of the few who never lost sight of her. Mort and Ysabell depart to begin married life as duke and duchess. Death, changed by his brief taste of living, of food, drink, and feeling, returns to his domain and resumes the unending duty of collecting souls, once again alone but no longer quite unmoved by the mortals he gathers.
recaps.in_short: Mort, a gawky farm boy, is apprenticed to Death and learns to collect the souls of the dying, living in Death's timeless domain with the servant Albert and Death's adopted daughter, Ysabell. When Death steps back to experience ordinary human life, he leaves the Duty to Mort, who is sent to gather the soul of Princess Keli of Sto Lat, marked for assassination. Smitten, Mort kills the assassin and saves her, but reality insists she should be dead and starts erasing her, sealing her kingdom inside a shrinking dome of altered history. With the wizard Cutwell and with Ysabell, Mort struggles to keep Keli alive and set history right, even as the work slowly turns him into something like Death himself. In the end Mort must fight Death to resolve it. Death spares him and repairs reality by his own hand, then dismisses him kindly: Mort marries Ysabell and is made Duke of Sto Helit, Keli keeps her throne, and Death returns to his solitary work.

recaps.text: At a hiring fair, the awkward, over-thoughtful farm boy Mort is taken on as an apprentice by Death, the robed skeleton who gathers the souls of the dying. Death brings him to his strange domain, a black house set in an ageless landscape with a garden of bone-white flowers, kept by the dry old servant Albert and shared with Death's adopted daughter, Ysabell. Mort learns the work: riding out on Death's horse, Binky, to be present at deaths and see souls safely on. Death, increasingly curious about living things, begins handing more of the duty to his apprentice so that he can go and explore what it is to be alive.

Left to perform the Duty alone while Death samples ordinary life, Mort is sent to collect the soul of Princess Keli of Sto Lat, who is fated to be murdered. Unable to stand by, he kills the assassin and saves her instead. This is a grave mistake: history knows Keli should be dead, and reality begins trying to correct itself, closing over her as people forget she exists. Mort seeks out the young wizard Cutwell, one of the few who can still perceive the princess, to help keep her alive while a shrinking dome of altered reality creeps in around her kingdom. Meanwhile Death throws himself into human pursuits, taking odd jobs and drinking, trying to feel what mortals feel.

The consequences of Mort's choice deepen. The pocket of true reality around Keli keeps contracting, and it becomes clear the wrong will not simply heal on its own. At the same time Mort himself is changing: performing Death's work is making him colder and more like his master, his eyes taking on a faint glow and his voice sometimes carrying Death's weight. Mort, Ysabell, and Cutwell search for a way to set history right without letting Keli die, while Death, having tasted mortality, proves oddly reluctant to resume his post. Thrown together by the crisis, Mort and Ysabell grow closer.

The reckoning arrives. To restore reality, Mort must confront Death directly, and the two duel with scythes. Death overcomes his apprentice but chooses to spare him, and rather than let the correction claim Keli's life he takes the burden onto himself and puts history right by his own means, dismissing Mort from his service in the process. The parting is generous: Death gives Mort and Ysabell his blessing to marry, and Keli, secure again on her throne, makes Mort a duke, granting him the dukedom of Sto Helit, while keeping Cutwell on as her royal recognizer. Mort and Ysabell leave to begin their life together, and Death, briefly touched by what he learned of living, returns alone to his endless duty.

characters.description: Fifteen, and no longer anyone's apprentice. She works cases as Skulduggery's partner, throws fire and shadows with equal confidence, and is still training in Necromancy under Solomon Wreath, which she has stopped bothering to hide and which Skulduggery has never once approved of. Her ordinary life in Haggard is lived by her mirror duplicate, and she notices less and less that this is not normal. She is stronger than most sorcerers twice her age and has begun to enjoy that fact.
characters.name: Valkyrie Cain

characters.description: The skeleton detective, back from the Faceless Ones' world and working again, with a Sanctuary that no longer treats him as a criminal. He is talking as much as ever and saying nothing at all about the months he spent on the other side of the portal, or about the war he fought before Valkyrie was born.
characters.name: Skulduggery Pleasant

characters.description: The English sword-fighter who walks on walls: Valkyrie's closest friend, cheerfully reckless, and the one person who treats her as an equal rather than as something to be protected or recruited.
characters.name: Tanith Low

characters.description: The scarred tailor, now an Elder of the Irish Sanctuary and visibly happier when he is in his shop than when he is in a council chamber. He can still turn his skin to stone and would still rather not have to.
characters.name: Ghastly Bespoke

characters.description: The Grand Mage of the Irish Sanctuary, one of the Dead Men and an old friend of Skulduggery's, running the place with a lighter hand than his predecessor and a good deal of political patience.
characters.name: Erskine Ravel

characters.description: The veiled Elder who speaks for the Children of the Spider, present at every Council meeting and volunteering nothing at any of them.
characters.name: Madame Mist

characters.description: The Teleporter, still able to step anywhere he can picture, and now Valkyrie's boyfriend, which is complicated by how much of her life he is not part of.
characters.name: Fletcher Renn

characters.description: The keeper of Dublin's great private library, still selling information to whoever pays and still declining to explain her own history with the people who worship the Faceless Ones.
characters.name: China Sorrows

characters.description: The elderly scientist who runs the medical facility behind the derelict cinema. He has spent years putting Valkyrie back together and telling her to stop, and he has never persuaded her of anything.
characters.name: Kenspeckle Grouse

characters.description: Kenspeckle Grouse's assistant: blue-haired, sweet-natured and entirely unbothered by the strangeness of the place she works in. She is fond of Valkyrie and of everyone else who comes through the door bleeding.
characters.name: Clarabelle

characters.description: The Necromancer who has been teaching Valkyrie the magic of shadow and death. Polite, unhurried and never quite finished making his case, he wants her inside his order and has told her that his people are waiting for the Death Bringer, who will end the division between the living and the dead.
characters.name: Solomon Wreath

characters.description: A tattooist and Sensitive, relaxed to the point of horizontal, who reads the future when it wanders into his head and would generally rather it did not. He has picked up something recently that has frightened him and everyone else who can see.
characters.name: Finbar Wrong

characters.description: A Sensitive who lives apart from the magical world and reads what is coming in steam and smoke. She is careful about what she says, because she has learned how much damage a half-understood vision can do.
characters.name: Cassandra Pharos

characters.description: A name out of the visions every Sensitive has been having: a sorcerer of overwhelming power who burns the world and laughs while doing it. Nobody knows who this person is, whether they are alive yet, or how long there is before the vision arrives.
characters.name: Darquesse

characters.description: A vampire who keeps away from the packs and holds himself under tighter control than his kind usually manage. Quiet, intense and old enough to be unnerving, he takes an interest in Valkyrie that she does not entirely discourage.
characters.name: Caelan

characters.description: The Texan killer with hollows where his eyes should be, who travels through solid ground and takes contracts from anyone. He turns up wherever there is money and disappears through the floor before anyone can arrest him.
characters.name: Billy-Ray Sanguine

characters.description: The Necromancer general who fought for Mevolent in black armour, disappeared before the war ended, and has recently begun killing again. His identity is still unknown, and he has been avoiding every attempt to corner him.
characters.name: Lord Vile

recaps.ending: The Remnants are driven back and contained, but the case ends with the ground moved under everyone. Kenspeckle Grouse is dead, killed during the outbreak, and Clarabelle is left running his facility without him. Valkyrie knows what the Sensitives were seeing: Darquesse is her true name, and the sorcerer who burns the world in every vision is her. She has been Darquesse once, briefly and completely, long enough to know how much she enjoyed it and how little of Valkyrie was left while it lasted, and long enough to have fought the thing in Lord Vile's armour to a standstill in front of witnesses. To make sure it cannot happen again, she has her true name sealed away, which should put Darquesse permanently out of reach. Skulduggery keeps the secret with her rather than reporting it. The worst blow is Tanith Low: as the Remnants are being rounded up, one takes her, and the possessed Tanith escapes with her own face, her own skill and none of her own loyalties. She is now somewhere in the world, on the other side, and she believes in Darquesse. Lord Vile's identity is still unexplained.
recaps.in_short: Sensitives, the sorcerers who see the future, are being murdered one after another, and every one of them had seen the same vision: a sorcerer called Darquesse destroying the world. While Skulduggery and Valkyrie investigate, a far more immediate threat gets loose, as thousands of Remnants, parasitic creatures that possess a host and unlock the worst of them, escape and sweep through Ireland, taking the Sanctuary and much of Dublin with them. Kenspeckle Grouse is killed in the outbreak. Valkyrie then learns what the visions meant: her true name is Darquesse. Speaking a true name unlocks everything a sorcerer can be, and when there is no other way to stop what is happening, Valkyrie becomes Darquesse, a being of enormous power and no restraint who fights the returned Lord Vile to a standstill before Valkyrie is brought back to herself. The Remnants are contained. Valkyrie has her true name sealed away so Darquesse cannot surface again, and Skulduggery helps her hide it. In the last moments, a Remnant takes Tanith Low, and the possessed Tanith escapes.

recaps.text: Previously: Stephanie Edgley became Valkyrie Cain, partner to the skeleton detective Skulduggery Pleasant in a hidden world of sorcerers. She killed Nefarian Serpine with the Sceptre of the Ancients, stopped Baron Vengeous from waking the Grotesquery, and learned that she is descended from the last of the Ancients. When the Diablerie opened a portal at Aranmore Farm, a Faceless One came through and killed the Sanctuary's Elders and Mr Bliss, and Skulduggery drove it back through the portal and was trapped in the dark gods' dead world. Valkyrie spent months getting him out, crossing over at last with the Teleporter Fletcher Renn and the Dead Men, Skulduggery's unit from the war. In the same case, Thurid Guild was removed as Grand Mage and replaced by Erskine Ravel, with Ghastly Bespoke and Madame Mist as Elders, and the armour of Lord Vile, a Necromancer general missing since the war, reappeared with an unknown wearer inside it who killed the Torment. Valkyrie has been training in Necromancy with Solomon Wreath, whose order is waiting for a figure of prophecy called the Death Bringer.

Sensitives, the sorcerers who see fragments of the future, are being killed. They are not a dangerous or a powerful group, which makes the murders difficult to explain, and Skulduggery and Valkyrie start work with no motive and a shrinking list of witnesses. Valkyrie is fifteen now, competent, busy, and living almost entirely on the magical side of her life while a duplicate handles school and her parents. Her Necromancy training with Solomon Wreath continues, to Skulduggery's steady disapproval, and the Sanctuary under Erskine Ravel is friendly enough to let them work without interference.

The reason for the killings turns out to be what the Sensitives have been seeing. All of them, independently, have had the same vision: a sorcerer called Darquesse, of overwhelming power, destroying the world and enjoying it. Nobody knows who Darquesse is or when it happens, and the people who have looked hardest at the vision have not survived long afterwards. Finbar Wrong and Cassandra Pharos, both Sensitives and both still alive, confirm the shape of it. It is not a warning that can be acted on, only one that can be feared, and it is now the most closely held secret in the magical world.

The investigation runs into a second and far more immediate danger: the Remnants. They are creatures without bodies of their own, thousands of them, kept sealed away for generations because a Remnant that reaches a person takes them over completely, wearing their face and their memories while removing every restraint they ever had. The victim is still in there and is no longer in charge. The seals do not hold. What begins as a handful of possessions becomes an outbreak, and the people it takes are people Valkyrie knows.

The Remnants sweep through Dublin and into the Sanctuary itself, and the institutions that are supposed to handle a crisis of this size are among the first things lost. Skulduggery, Valkyrie, Ghastly, Tanith and Ravel are reduced to a small group of people who can still be trusted to be themselves, fighting former colleagues who cannot be killed without killing the host. Kenspeckle Grouse is killed during the outbreak, leaving Clarabelle alone in the facility behind the cinema. There is no reinforcement coming and no obvious way to put thousands of Remnants back where they came from.

Valkyrie learns what the visions were about. Every sorcerer has a true name, the word that is what they actually are, and speaking it unlocks the whole of their potential and hands anyone who knows it total power over them. Hers is Darquesse. The being who burns the world in every Sensitive's vision is not a stranger to be hunted down and stopped in advance; it is her, waiting inside her name. Skulduggery, who has reasons of his own for understanding what a person can become, keeps it quiet rather than handing it to the Sanctuary, and Valkyrie has to decide what to do with a truth she cannot give back.

With the Remnants winning and nothing left that works, Valkyrie's true name is unlocked and Darquesse takes over. She is immensely, casually powerful, indifferent to everyone she was fond of an hour earlier, and delighted with herself. Lord Vile comes for her, and the two of them fight without either being able to finish it, the first time anyone has seen what is in the armour tested at that level. Valkyrie is eventually brought back to herself, with the memory of everything Darquesse did and, worse, of how much she enjoyed being her.

The Remnants are driven back and sealed away again, at a cost the Sanctuary spends years counting. Kenspeckle Grouse is dead. Valkyrie, unwilling to risk Darquesse ever surfacing again, has her true name sealed so that it cannot be spoken or used, by her or by anyone else, and Skulduggery helps her keep the whole business off the record. It should be finished. Then, as the last of the outbreak is being cleared up, a Remnant takes Tanith Low. The possessed Tanith walks out with her own face, her own skill with a sword and none of her own loyalties, and disappears, leaving Valkyrie without her closest friend and the world with a very capable new enemy who is certain that Darquesse is coming. Lord Vile's identity remains unknown.

characters.description: A young mouse who walks into Mossflower out of the north, ragged, half-starved and carrying an old sword that belonged to his father, Luke the Warrior. He has been a wanderer for a long time and has learned to fight the hard way. Plain-spoken, obstinate and slow to trust, he wants nothing to do with anyone else's war until the wildcats of Kotir take his sword and put him in their dungeon, at which point their war becomes his.
characters.name: Martin

characters.description: An old wildcat warlord who conquered Mossflower long ago and rules it from the fortress of Kotir, taxing the woodlanders for tribute they can barely spare. Once a formidable soldier, he is now visibly ill and rarely leaves his chamber, and his two grown children are already circling the question of who will hold Kotir after him.
characters.name: Verdauga Greeneyes

characters.description: Verdauga's daughter, a powerful young wildcat, quick, violent and utterly without patience. She commands her father's soldiers in the field, despises the woodlanders as vermin to be worked and taxed, and makes no secret of thinking that Kotir is being run far too softly. Her one weakness is a terror of deep water that she will not admit to.
characters.name: Tsarmina

characters.description: Verdauga's son and Tsarmina's brother, a wildcat who has no appetite for his family's trade. He argues for leaving the woodlanders alone and would rather Kotir made peace than tribute, which makes him useless to his sister and an obstacle to her plans.
characters.name: Gingivere

characters.description: A plump, irrepressible mouse who calls himself the Prince of Mousethieves, a singer, a mimic and a genuinely gifted burglar who steals mainly from Kotir and mainly for the fun of it. He is in the fortress dungeon when Martin arrives there, and his talent for getting into and out of places he should not be becomes the woodlanders' greatest asset. He treats every crisis as an opportunity for a song.
characters.name: Gonff

characters.description: A vixen who serves Kotir as its healer and adviser. She is competent, cold and entirely self-interested, and she is willing to be useful to whichever wildcat ends up holding the fortress.
characters.name: Fortunata

characters.description: A pine marten, stiff-legged since an old injury, who serves as one of Kotir's senior officers and advisers. Cautious where his mistress is reckless, he spends much of his effort avoiding blame and avoiding the enormous old eagle who has been trying to eat him for seasons.
characters.name: Ashleg

characters.description: A hedgehog of Mossflower with a family to feed and a farm to work, who has paid Kotir's tribute for years and is close to the end of his patience. He is one of the first woodlanders to shelter escapers from the fortress.
characters.name: Ben Stickle

characters.description: A badger, the keeper of Brockhall, the great hidden dwelling beneath the roots of Mossflower where the woodlanders meet in secret. Wise, deliberate and widely respected, she is the closest thing the scattered creatures of the wood have to a leader. Her father left Mossflower long ago for a mountain in the west and never returned.
characters.name: Bella of Brockhall

characters.description: A young mousemaid of the Mossflower woodlanders, sensible and steady, who helps run the household at Brockhall and keeps the resistance supplied. She takes an immediate and long-suffering interest in Gonff.
characters.name: Columbine

characters.description: A young mole with a broad country accent, enormous digging claws and complete unflappability. He becomes the third member of Martin and Gonff's company, on the grounds that no journey should be attempted without a mole.
characters.name: Dinny

characters.description: The leader of Mossflower's moles, a slow-spoken and immovable engineer who understands earth, water and tunnels better than anyone alive. What he can do with a shovel and a season's planning eventually matters more than any weapon the woodlanders own.
characters.name: Foremole

characters.description: The chieftain of Mossflower's squirrels, a hard-eyed archer who leads her people through the treetops and raids Kotir's patrols from above. She is one of the resistance's three field commanders.
characters.name: Lady Amber

characters.description: The chieftain of the otters of the river, cheerful, loud and dangerous with a sling. His crew handles the water and provides much of the muscle in the woodlanders' campaign against the fortress.
characters.name: Skipper

characters.description: The leader of a tribe of shrews who quarrel constantly and travel the waterways in logboats. His name is the title of whoever leads them. He is met on the road west and proves both a difficult ally and an indispensable one.
characters.name: Log-a-Log

characters.description: The badger lord of Salamandastron, the fire mountain on the western shore, and Bella's long-vanished father. He is an enormous, scarred fighter and a master smith, and he lives with the certainty of his own fate at the mountain. The hares of the mountain follow him absolutely.
characters.name: Boar the Fighter

characters.description: The leader of a community of mice from the distant abbey of Loamhedge, an elderly, practical and very determined mouse who arrives in Mossflower looking for somewhere her people can settle and build.
characters.name: Germaine

recaps.ending: The moles' channels do their work and the river pours into the diggings beneath Kotir. The fortress floods and sinks, its stones settling into a new lake, and the garrison scatters; Ashleg and Fortunata abandon their mistress and slip away. Tsarmina, who has feared deep water all her life, is left facing Martin as her stronghold goes under, and she drowns in the flood that takes Kotir. Gingivere, freed from the cell his sister put him in, is given his life and goes north to live quietly on a farm, wanting nothing further to do with conquest. Mossflower is free for the first time in a generation, and the woodlanders begin quarrying the stones of the drowned fortress for something to build with. Germaine and the mice of Loamhedge, who arrived looking for a home, join them, and together they start raising an abbey beside the road through the woods, a house intended to shelter and feed anyone who comes to it: Redwall. Martin hangs up the sword Boar forged for him and takes the role of the new abbey's protector rather than a warlord's. Gonff and Columbine marry, and the story closes on the first stones of the abbey going up.
recaps.in_short: Mossflower Wood is held by the wildcats of the fortress Kotir, where the ailing warlord Verdauga rules until his daughter Tsarmina takes the fortress for herself, imprisons her brother Gingivere and tightens her grip on the woodlanders. Martin, a wandering young mouse, is captured, has his father's sword broken by Tsarmina and is thrown into the dungeons, where he meets the thief Gonff. The two escape and join the woodland resistance based at Brockhall under Bella the badger, who tells Martin of her father, Boar the Fighter, lord of the mountain Salamandastron in the west. Martin, Gonff and Dinny the mole travel west to seek his help, gathering allies on the road, and at the mountain Boar forges Martin a new sword from star metal before dying in a battle against sea rats. While they are away, the woodlanders starve Kotir out and the moles dig channels to turn the river against it. Martin returns as the fortress floods and sinks, and Tsarmina, terrified of water all her life, drowns with it. On the ruins the freed woodlanders and a company of mice from Loamhedge begin building Redwall Abbey.

recaps.text: This story is set generations before Redwall Abbey exists. Everything a listener needs is introduced here; no earlier book is required. It is worth knowing only that Martin the Warrior is the figure Redwall later remembers as its founding protector, the mouse whose sword hangs in the Abbey's hall in the books set long afterwards, and that the wood the story takes place in is the same Mossflower that surrounds the Abbey in those later tales.

Mossflower Wood is occupied territory. The wildcat warlord Verdauga Greeneyes holds it from Kotir, a fortress garrisoned by weasels, stoats, ferrets and rats, and the woodlanders pay tribute they cannot afford. Verdauga is old and ill, and his two children are already positioning themselves: his daughter Tsarmina, who commands the soldiers and thinks her father far too lenient, and his son Gingivere, who would rather Kotir left the woodlanders in peace. Into this walks Martin, a young mouse travelling south, ragged and armed with the sword his father left him. He is taken by a Kotir patrol, brought before the wildcats, and refuses to submit. Tsarmina breaks his sword in front of him and has him thrown into the fortress dungeons to die there.

In the cells Martin meets Gonff, a cheerful mouse thief who has been stealing from Kotir for seasons and treats imprisonment as a temporary inconvenience. Above them, Tsarmina moves: Verdauga dies, and she takes the fortress, blaming her brother for the death and having Gingivere locked away. She proclaims herself ruler of Mossflower and sets about squeezing the woodlanders harder, with the vixen Fortunata and the pine marten Ashleg as her chief officers. Martin and Gonff break out of the dungeons and reach Brockhall, the hidden hall beneath the roots of the wood, where the woodlanders shelter. There Bella the badger, Columbine, the hedgehog Ben Stickle and the rest have been enduring rather than resisting. Martin's arrival, and the loss of his sword, turns their endurance into a decision to fight.

The woodlanders begin a campaign they cannot win outright: Lady Amber's squirrels shoot from the treetops, Skipper's otters raid from the water, and Gonff robs Kotir's stores repeatedly. The strategy is to make the fortress feed itself and then stop it doing so. Tsarmina's patrols come back beaten or not at all, and her officers start hiding bad news from her. Small victories are paid for with real losses, and Kotir still stands, too strong to storm and too well built to burn. Bella tells Martin about her father, Boar the Fighter, who left Mossflower long ago for Salamandastron, the mountain of badger lords on the western shore, and never came back. If anyone can give the woodlanders the strength to finish Kotir, it is Boar.

Martin agrees to go west and find Boar. Gonff refuses to be left behind, and Dinny the mole joins on the principle that the pair of them will walk into a hole without him. They leave Mossflower with directions that amount to guesswork. Behind them, the woodlanders keep up the raids and Tsarmina grows more erratic, seeing treachery everywhere and driving her own officers away from her. Kotir's stores dwindle through the season, and the fortress that was built to hold a wood down starts to look like a place under siege by the wood itself. Foremole and his crews begin surveying the ground around the fortress with an idea that has nothing to do with weapons.

The journey west is long and dangerous. Martin, Gonff and Dinny cross unfamiliar country, are hunted, taken in and threatened by turns, and fall in with Log-a-Log and his quarrelsome shrews, who become allies after a difficult start. They survive encounters with creatures who treat travellers as sport and are helped by others who have no reason to help them at all. The three of them are held together mainly by Gonff's refusal to be discouraged and Martin's refusal to turn back. Eventually the land begins to slope down toward the western shore, and ahead of them stands the mountain: Salamandastron, hollowed out and inhabited, held by badger lords and their hares.

At Salamandastron they find Boar the Fighter, Bella's father, an enormous scarred badger who rules the mountain with its company of hares. He will not come back to Mossflower: he knows a sea rat fleet is coming and he intends to meet it at his own mountain, and he speaks about his own end as something already settled. What he gives Martin instead is a sword, forged in the mountain's own furnace from metal that fell out of the sky, balanced for a mouse and better than anything Martin has ever held. Then the sea rats land, the mountain is besieged, and Boar leads its defence with the hares behind him while Martin, Gonff and Dinny are caught up in a battle that was never theirs.

Salamandastron holds, but Boar the Fighter dies there in the fighting, having sent Martin and his companions away from the mountain before the end. Martin turns for home carrying the sword Boar made him and the news Bella will not want to hear. The return journey is made in company, with the shrews' logboats and allies gathered along the way, and Martin arrives back in a Mossflower that has changed. Kotir is starving. Tsarmina's soldiers are deserting, her officers are avoiding her, and she is close to breaking under the pressure of a war she cannot bring to battle. The woodlanders have not been idle either: Foremole and his moles have spent the season digging, and their tunnels are not for hiding in. They are channels, dug to bring the river in under the fortress. Everything is now in place for an ending that does not depend on storming Kotir's walls at all.

The moles open the channels and the water comes. Kotir floods and settles into the ground, becoming a lake, and the garrison scatters, Ashleg and Fortunata among them. Tsarmina, whose one real fear has always been deep water, faces Martin as her fortress goes under and drowns in the flood. Gingivere is released from his cell, spared, and goes north to live quietly as a farmer. Mossflower is free. The woodlanders begin lifting the drowned fortress's stone for a building of their own, and are joined by Germaine and her community of mice from the distant abbey of Loamhedge, who have come looking for a home. Together they start raising an abbey beside the woodland road, meant to shelter and feed anyone who needs it, and they name it Redwall. Martin hangs up his sword and becomes its protector rather than its lord, and Gonff and Columbine marry as the first walls go up.

characters.description: A student wizard at Unseen University who has spent years deliberately not graduating. His late uncle's legacy pays his fees only for as long as he remains a student, so he must score high enough in his examinations to avoid being thrown out and low enough to avoid passing, and he has worked out precisely which mark achieves both. The effort of maintaining this has left him extraordinarily fit, well read and quick-witted, and entirely without ambition. When a strange restlessness begins pulling people toward a stretch of coast called Holy Wood, he goes.
characters.name: Victor Tugelbend

characters.description: An alchemist of Ankh-Morpork whose experiments with octo-cellulose produce the first moving pictures on the Disc. Enthusiastic, technically minded and not remotely interested in stories, he sees the invention as a scientific achievement and is baffled and then sidelined when other people see it as an industry.
characters.name: Thomas Silverfish

characters.description: The keeper of Unseen University's library and an orangutan, a shape he acquired in a magical accident and has firmly declined to give up. He reads the University's instruments, notices that something is badly wrong with the magical background of the world, and is one of the few who take it seriously. He communicates in a single syllable and is enormously strong.
characters.name: The Librarian

characters.description: A very old wizard of Unseen University, kept alive largely by habit, whose memory reaches back further than anyone else's on the faculty. Deaf, cheerful and easily distracted, he nonetheless remembers fragments of things the University has forgotten.
characters.name: Windle Poons

characters.description: The newly elected Archchancellor of Unseen University, brought in from a country estate where he had spent decades hunting, fishing and shouting at things. Loud, hearty and physically robust in a way the faculty finds deeply upsetting, he has no patience with committees, ceremony or the University's tradition of murdering its way up the hierarchy, and he takes an interest in whatever is going on outside the walls.
characters.name: Mustrum Ridcully

characters.description: A young woman from a small town who has come to Holy Wood determined to become a star, and who has more drive and more raw talent for the work than anyone else there. Sharp, ambitious and impatient, she uses the name Ginger rather than the one she was born with.
characters.name: Theda Withel

characters.description: Ankh-Morpork's most persistent street trader, seller of sausages of uncertain composition, who follows the crowd to Holy Wood and reinvents himself as a maker of moving pictures. He understands nothing about the craft and everything about an audience, and he grasps faster than anyone that the point of the business is not the pictures but what can be sold alongside them.
characters.name: Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler

characters.description: A small, filthy, disreputable mongrel with a permanent cough and an extremely low opinion of humanity. The strange magic around Holy Wood has given him speech, and he has worked out that being a talking dog is worth far less than being a dog people underestimate. He is cynical, self-interested, and rather more decent in practice than he would ever admit.
characters.name: Gaspode the Wonder Dog

characters.description: A large troll who comes to Holy Wood looking for work, having previously made a living removing unwanted customers from taverns. He thinks slowly in warm weather and finds the picture business confusing, but he is reliable, literal and immensely strong, and he takes to the trade of being hit by things for money.
characters.name: Detritus

characters.description: A landlady in Holy Wood who rents rooms to the new arrivals and is entirely unimpressed by any of them. She is practical, blunt and full of firm sayings about hard work and thrift, which she delivers to anyone standing still long enough.
characters.name: Mrs Marietta Cosmopilite

characters.description: A handsome, golden, magnificently stupid dog who is made into a canine star, performing rescues and heroics for the cameras. Every clever thing he appears to do is worked out for him in advance by Gaspode, who resents the arrangement considerably.
characters.name: Laddie

characters.description: A troll singer working in Holy Wood, large, glittering and possessed of a voice that stops rooms. Detritus is entirely undone by her, and she is prepared to be patient about it.
characters.name: Ruby

characters.description: Dibbler's nephew, who does the actual work of organising and directing the pictures while his uncle handles the selling. Younger, more capable and far more interested in the craft, he keeps the productions running in spite of the promises made on their behalf.
characters.name: Soll Dibbler

recaps.ending: At the premiere of the great epic in Ankh-Morpork the barrier finally fails. The presence buried beneath Holy Wood takes Ginger completely, and she grows to enormous size and climbs the Tower of Art carrying the Librarian, while creatures from the Dungeon Dimensions force their way through into the city. Victor climbs after her, breaks the hold on her, and turns the logic of Holy Wood back against what is using it, and the way through is shut. Holy Wood does not survive it. The town is destroyed and the sand begins to cover it again, and with the magic gone the whole industry collapses as suddenly as it appeared: the pictures stop working, the crowds go home, and the people who were stars a week earlier are simply people again. Dibbler goes back to Ankh-Morpork and to selling sausages, already thinking about the next thing. Detritus and Ruby stay together and leave for the city. Gaspode keeps his voice, and his opinions. Victor and Ginger, no longer famous and no longer needed, walk away from the ruins together. The wizards return to Unseen University under their new Archchancellor with the affair closed, and the hill above Holy Wood is quiet again.
recaps.in_short: When the last keeper of an ancient rite at Holy Wood dies with no successor, something long buried under the hill begins to wake. In Ankh-Morpork the alchemist Thomas Silverfish invents moving pictures, and within weeks half the city feels an inexplicable urge to travel to Holy Wood and make them. Among them are Victor Tugelbend, a student wizard who has spent years avoiding graduation, and Ginger, a determined young woman who becomes the Disc's first leading lady. A boom town rises overnight, run by Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler; trolls, dwarfs and a talking dog named Gaspode pour in. But the pictures work because reality is thin at Holy Wood, and every audience that watches them makes it thinner. Ginger sleepwalks to a buried door beneath the hill. At the premiere of Dibbler's enormous epic the barrier gives way: Ginger is taken over and grows gigantic, climbing the Tower of Art with the Librarian, while things from outside reality pour into the city. Victor frees her and closes the way. Holy Wood burns, the industry vanishes overnight, and the sand covers the hill again.

recaps.text: On a stretch of empty coast called Holy Wood, an old man dies. He was the last of a line of keepers whose only duty was to perform a rite that kept something beneath the hill asleep, and there is no one to take his place. Not long afterwards, in Ankh-Morpork, the alchemist Thomas Silverfish stumbles on a way of capturing moving images: strips of octo-cellulose and small, very fast imps that paint what they see. The invention is a curiosity for about a week. Then people across the city begin to feel a pull they cannot explain, a conviction that they must go to Holy Wood, and they start walking. Among them is Victor Tugelbend, a student wizard at Unseen University who has spent years scoring exactly high enough not to be expelled and exactly low enough not to graduate, because his uncle's legacy pays only while he remains a student. He abandons the arrangement and heads for the coast.

Holy Wood becomes a boom town almost overnight: shacks, lots, handlemen turning the cranks of picture boxes, and a constant stream of new arrivals, human, dwarf and troll. Victor drifts into work as an extra and is quickly recognised as a natural leading man. He meets Ginger, a young woman from a small town who has come with the single-minded intention of becoming a star and has the talent to manage it, and the two are paired in picture after picture. Cut-Me-Own-Throat Dibbler, Ankh-Morpork's most tireless street trader, arrives, sees the possibilities immediately, and sets himself up as a producer. Nobody in Holy Wood asks why the place exists or why everyone felt compelled to come, and nobody notices that things there are becoming a little too much like a story.

The industry grows at a speed nobody controls. Dozens of short pictures are made every week, audiences form in every town, and Ankh-Morpork gets its first picture house. Ginger and Victor become the two most recognisable faces on the Disc. The magic soaking the place has side effects: animals begin to talk, among them Gaspode, a scruffy and deeply cynical mongrel who quickly decides that concealing his speech is more profitable than displaying it. Gaspode ends up ghost-thinking for Laddie, a handsome and entirely stupid dog who is made a canine star. Detritus, a troll looking for work, finds it, and finds Ruby, a troll singer, at the same time. Meanwhile Ginger has begun sleepwalking, leaving her lodgings at night and walking to the old hill above the town, and she remembers none of it in the morning.

Victor follows Ginger on one of her night walks and finds that she has been digging, and that beneath the hill there is a door and, behind it, a buried chamber older than any history Holy Wood has. He begins looking into what the place actually is, and finds traces of an earlier civilisation that made pictures here before, and of the keepers who spent centuries afterwards making sure nothing was disturbed. At Unseen University the instruments are showing something badly wrong, and the Librarian, who has been watching them, sets out for the coast. The new Archchancellor, Mustrum Ridcully, is dragged into the question by the readings and by the recollections of the very elderly Windle Poons, who remembers fragments of things the University has otherwise lost. Dibbler, indifferent to all of it, announces that he will make the largest picture ever attempted.

The wizards work out the shape of the danger. Holy Wood sits where the wall between the world and the Dungeon Dimensions is thin, and the pictures are not merely entertainment: an audience believing hard enough in what it sees is an opening, and every showing widens it. The creatures on the other side have been feeding on that belief and shaping what people want to watch. Ginger's sleepwalking is the buried presence reaching for a body. Filming of Dibbler's epic goes ahead at enormous scale and enormous expense, with elephants, thousands of extras and a budget that exists mainly as promises, and things begin to appear on the film that nobody put there. Victor and Ginger try to warn people and are ignored, because the show is now too large to stop, and the premiere is set for Ankh-Morpork.

The premiere fills the city. As the picture runs, the belief of the audience does exactly what the wizards feared, and reality gives way. Creatures from the Dungeon Dimensions come through into Ankh-Morpork, and the presence beneath Holy Wood takes Ginger entirely. She grows to enormous size, seizes the Librarian, and begins climbing the Tower of Art at the heart of Unseen University while the city watches from below, and the wizards and the Watch can do nothing that makes any difference. Victor, who now understands that Holy Wood runs on the logic of stories and that whatever is coming through needs a story in order to arrive, goes up the tower after her.

At the top of the tower Victor breaks the hold the buried presence has over Ginger and turns Holy Wood's own logic against the things using it, and the way between the worlds is shut. Ginger returns to her own size and her own mind, and the creatures are driven back. Holy Wood itself does not survive: the town is destroyed and the sand begins to bury the hill again. With the magic gone the entire industry collapses at once. The pictures stop working, the crowds disperse, and everyone who was famous a week ago is ordinary again. Dibbler returns to Ankh-Morpork and his sausage tray, already considering his next venture. Detritus and Ruby leave together for the city. Gaspode keeps his voice and his poor opinion of everyone. Victor and Ginger, free of fame and of the thing that made it, leave the ruins together, and the wizards go back to the University with the matter closed.

characters.description: A celebrated Belgian detective, small, immaculate, and vain of his moustaches, travelling back from a case in the East and anxious to reach London. He works by talking to people and weighing what they choose to say against what they cannot help revealing, and he is far more interested in character than in cigarette ash. Chapter positions in this entry follow the book's three parts read straight through, so Part Two chapter one is counted as chapter nine.
characters.name: Hercule Poirot

characters.description: A young Englishwoman travelling home from Baghdad, where she has been a governess. Cool, competent, and strikingly self-possessed under discomfort and delay, she manages her own affairs without fuss. Poirot notices her calm on the Taurus Express and also a moment when it deserts her.
characters.name: Mary Debenham

characters.description: A British Army officer on leave from India, correct, reticent, and given to short declarative opinions and a pipe. He is protective of Miss Debenham, whom he meets on the journey from Syria, and disapproves of discussing other people's business.
characters.name: Colonel Arbuthnot

characters.description: A director of the company that runs the international sleeping cars and an old friend of Poirot, genial, excitable, and fond of a good dinner. He arranges a berth for Poirot on a train that should have been empty and is not, and later asks him to take charge of the investigation to spare the company a scandal.
characters.name: Monsieur Bouc

characters.description: A wealthy elderly American travelling with a secretary and a valet, said to be in business of an unspecified kind. He has a pleasant manner and, as Poirot observes him, an expression that does not match it. Believing himself in danger, he offers Poirot a large sum to act as his bodyguard, and is refused.
characters.name: Samuel Edward Ratchett

characters.description: Ratchett's private secretary and interpreter, a friendly young American who speaks no language but his own and is glad of company on a long journey. He handles his employer's correspondence and travel arrangements, and admits without much prompting that he does not like the man he works for.
characters.name: Hector MacQueen

characters.description: Ratchett's English valet, correct, colourless, and answering questions in the fewest words a servant can use. He suffers from toothache on the journey and shares a compartment with another passenger.
characters.name: Edward Masterman

characters.description: A talkative middle-aged American woman travelling home from a visit to her daughter, with strong views on foreigners, sanitation, and the conduct of railways, which she shares with everyone in the coach. Her compartment adjoins Ratchett's, and she is convinced that a man was in it during the night.
characters.name: Mrs Hubbard

characters.description: An ancient and formidable Russian aristocrat, tiny, ugly, and entirely unbothered by either fact, travelling with her own maid. She speaks with the bluntness of someone who has not had to be tactful for sixty years and expects to be obeyed.
characters.name: Princess Dragomiroff

characters.description: A young and beautiful Hungarian woman travelling with her husband, quiet, foreign-educated, and content to let him answer for her. She keeps to her compartment for most of the journey.
characters.name: Countess Elena Andrenyi

characters.description: A Hungarian diplomat travelling with his wife on a diplomatic passport, courteous, guarded, and quick to invoke his privileges when questions become personal.
characters.name: Count Rudolph Andrenyi

characters.description: A middle-aged Swedish woman returning from missionary work, trained as a nurse and easily reduced to tears by any unkindness. Her English is uncertain and her anxiety to be helpful is considerable.
characters.name: Greta Ohlsson

characters.description: A large, cheerful Italian-American who has lived many years in the United States and sells motor cars. He talks readily, gestures a great deal, and shares a compartment with Ratchett's valet, whose reserve he finds trying.
characters.name: Antonio Foscarelli

characters.description: A large American travelling as a salesman of typewriter ribbons, loud, friendly, and in the corridor a good deal. His account of himself does not survive Poirot's first serious question.
characters.name: Cyrus Hardman

characters.description: Princess Dragomiroff's German lady's maid, middle-aged, respectable, and frightened of officials. She is devoted to her mistress and gives her evidence with obvious nervousness.
characters.name: Hildegarde Schmidt

characters.description: The French conductor of the Istanbul to Calais coach, a long-serving employee of the sleeping-car company, responsible for the passengers, the bells, and the door to the next carriage. He is on duty in the corridor for most of the night.
characters.name: Pierre Michel

characters.description: A Greek doctor travelling in the same coach, who examines the body and works out what he can about the wounds and the time of death. He assists Poirot and Monsieur Bouc throughout the enquiry and is inclined to believe whatever the medical evidence suggests, even when it contradicts itself.
characters.name: Dr Constantine

recaps.ending: Poirot works out that every passenger in the Istanbul to Calais coach is connected to the Armstrong household. Mrs Hubbard is the actress Linda Arden, Daisy Armstrong's grandmother; the Countess Andrenyi is Daisy's aunt, and her husband altered her passport to hide it; Mary Debenham was the child's governess and Greta Ohlsson her nurse; Princess Dragomiroff was godmother to Daisy's mother; Hildegarde Schmidt was the family's cook and Masterman Colonel Armstrong's soldier servant; Foscarelli was their chauffeur; Colonel Arbuthnot was Armstrong's friend from the war; MacQueen was the son of the district attorney who prosecuted the case; Hardman was a detective in love with the accused nursemaid; and Pierre Michel, the conductor, was her father. Twelve of them stabbed Ratchett once each, in the dark, so that none could know whose blow was fatal, a jury carrying out the sentence the courts never delivered. The confusing evidence, the varying wounds, the smashed watch, the woman in the scarlet kimono and the stranger in a conductor's uniform were all planted to support a story about an outsider. Poirot lays two solutions before Monsieur Bouc and Dr Constantine: an unknown assassin who boarded at the stop and left again, or the truth. They choose the first, and Poirot says that having offered his solutions he takes his leave of the case. The snowplough clears the line and the train goes on with the Yugoslav police to be given the convenient explanation.
recaps.in_short: Returning urgently to London, Hercule Poirot boards the Simplon Orient Express at Istanbul and finds it inexplicably full for the time of year. Among the passengers is an American named Ratchett, who offers Poirot money to protect him from enemies and is refused. That night the train is stopped by a snowdrift in the Balkans, and in the morning Ratchett is found stabbed a dozen times behind a locked door. A charred scrap of paper identifies him as Cassetti, the man who kidnapped and murdered the child Daisy Armstrong in America and escaped punishment on a technicality. Investigating for the sleeping-car company, Poirot finds the evidence absurdly abundant and contradictory: wounds struck with different hands and force, a scarlet kimono, a conductor's uniform, a stopped watch, and an alibi for every passenger. He eventually establishes that all of them are connected to the Armstrong household, and that twelve of them stabbed the man once each, as a jury and executioners. Poirot offers two explanations and allows the innocuous one, an outside assassin, to be given to the police.

recaps.text: Hercule Poirot leaves Syria after a case and travels by the Taurus Express towards Istanbul, sharing the journey with an English governess, Mary Debenham, and Colonel Arbuthnot, an army officer coming from India. A telegram at Istanbul recalls him to London at once, and his friend Monsieur Bouc, a director of the sleeping-car company, secures him a berth on the Simplon Orient Express although the coach is unaccountably full for the time of year. The passengers include the American Ratchett, his secretary MacQueen and his valet Masterman, the talkative Mrs Hubbard, an aged Russian princess and her maid, a Hungarian count and countess, a Swedish nurse, an Italian-American car salesman, an American commercial traveller, and Debenham and Arbuthnot. Ratchett tells Poirot that he has received threatening letters and offers a large fee for protection; Poirot declines. In the night Poirot is woken repeatedly by bells, a cry from the next compartment, a woman in a scarlet kimono in the corridor, and the sensation of the train coming to a stand. By morning the express is buried in a snowdrift somewhere in Yugoslavia, and Ratchett is found dead in his locked compartment, stabbed many times over.
